excerpt: Sendbird provides chat, voice and video APIs for apps and an AI customer experience platform called delight.ai. Founded in 2013, valued at $1.05 billion in 2021.
content:
Sendbird sells communication infrastructure for apps. Developers add its chat API and SDKs to put in-app messaging, group chat, voice and video calls, business messaging and content moderation into their own products without building a messaging backend. More recently it has moved into AI customer service: its website now leads with delight.ai, an AI concierge for personalised customer experiences across the customer journey, alongside a support agent desk and a Salesforce connector. Y Combinator's directory quotes the company as saying the platform has more than 300 million monthly active users.

Sendbird was founded in 2013 and went through Y Combinator in winter 2016; it is based in San Francisco, and John S. Kim is cofounder and CEO. Before Sendbird, Kim founded Paprika Lab, a social gaming company. In April 2021 Sendbird raised a $100 million Series C at a $1.05 billion valuation, led by STEADFAST Capital Ventures with Emergence Capital, SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and World Innovation Lab joining earlier backers ICONIQ Growth, Tiger Global and Meritech, PYMNTS and KoreaTechDesk reported; KoreaTechDesk called it Korea's first B2B enterprise software unicorn. At the time Sendbird said 150 million users sent more than 2.5 billion messages a month on its platform.

Sendbird's pricing page offers a free trial and Starter, Pro and Enterprise chat plans priced by monthly active users; enterprise and AI products are quoted by sales.

We have not used Sendbird for this page. It brings together Sendbird's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
